title: POST /steps/:key/complete is idempotent for a repeated call on the same step
description: onboarding.controller.js completeStep uses $addToSet on completedSteps, so calling the same step twice must not create a duplicate array entry or change the currentStep result.
preconditions: Authenticated onboarding session (bootstrap JWT) for a fresh org at step-1
expectedResult: completedSteps contains exactly one 'step-1' entry after both calls; currentStep is 'step-2' both times; the second call returns 200, not an error.

title: GET /onboarding/state auto-provisions a fresh OnboardingState document when none exists
description: getState() (onboarding.controller.js lines 31-35) creates { orgId, currentStep:'step-1', completedSteps:[] } on the fly if no document is found — relevant for orgs provisioned outside the normal signup transaction (e.g. legacy/DIY-migrated orgs).
preconditions: An org exists with no onboarding_state document at all
steps: As a user of that org, call GET /api/v1/onboarding/state
expectedResult: Response is 200 with currentStep:'step-1', completedSteps: [], setupHealthScore: 0 — and a document is now persisted for subsequent calls.

title: All /api/v1/onboarding/* routes return 404 when isPricingOnboardingV1Enabled() is off
description: onboarding.routes.js line 21-26 short-circuits every route (including public ones like /signup and /frameworks) with 404 NOT_FOUND when the pricing-onboarding-v1 feature flag is disabled, forcing legacy signup instead.
preconditions: Feature flag isPricingOnboardingV1Enabled() forced to false
expectedResult: All three calls return 404 { error: { code: 'NOT_FOUND' } } — including the otherwise-public /frameworks and /signup endpoints.

title: Completing an unknown step key is rejected before any database write
expectedResult: The complete call returns 400 { error: { code: 'INVALID_STEP', message: 'Unknown step: step-99' } }; the subsequent GET shows completedSteps unchanged.

title: Step-4 completes even when the bulk-invite call fails
description: step-4/page.jsx wraps the POST /users/bulk-invite call in .catch(() => {/* quota — non-fatal */}) so a seat-limit or quota failure on the invite endpoint must not block onboardingService.completeStep('step-4', ...) from running afterward.
preconditions: Org is at its seat limit so POST /users/bulk-invite would reject additional invites
steps: On /onboarding/step-4, add 2 teammate emails and submit
Observe the bulk-invite API response (expected to fail/reject due to seat limit)
Observe the subsequent onboarding step-4 completion call and navigation
expectedResult: Despite the bulk-invite failure, POST /steps/step-4/complete still fires and succeeds, and the wizard advances to /onboarding/step-5.

title: POST /onboarding/signup creates Organization, User, OnboardingState and a default Project in a single transaction
description: signup.controller.js _withTxn() wraps Organization.create, User.create, OnboardingState.create, and Project.createWithCode. A duplicate email or domain must roll back the whole transaction and surface a 409.
preconditions: An organization already exists with domain 'acme.com'
steps: POST /api/v1/onboarding/signup with domain='acme.com' and a new email
POST /api/v1/onboarding/signup again reusing an email that already exists on any org
expectedResult: First call returns 409 { error: { code: 'DOMAIN_TAKEN' } } with no partial Organization/User/OnboardingState/Project rows created. Second call (existing email, new domain) returns 409 { error: { code: 'EMAIL_TAKEN' } } under the same rollback guarantee.

title: Keycloak user creation failure rolls back the Mongo records created during signup
description: signup.controller.js lines 156-177: if _createKeycloakUser throws, the handler deletes the just-created Organization, User, OnboardingState, and Project documents and returns 502 KEYCLOAK_SYNC_FAILED.
preconditions: Keycloak admin API mocked to reject user creation
steps: Observe the Keycloak failure and the response
Query Mongo directly for the Organization/User/OnboardingState/Project just referenced by orgId
expectedResult: Response is 502 { error: { code: 'KEYCLOAK_SYNC_FAILED' } } and none of the 4 Mongo documents remain — the org is not left in a half-provisioned state.

title: Platform tour status/update is isolated per user within the same organization
description: PlatformTourState (platform-tour-state.model.js) is keyed uniquely on userId, not orgId — two users in the same org must have completely independent introDone/tourDone/tourSelection state.
preconditions: User A and User B belong to the same organization
User A has already completed the platform tour (tourDone=true)
steps: As User B (same org, never toured), GET /api/v1/onboarding/platform-tour/status
expectedResult: User A's response shows tourDone: true. User B's response shows introDone: false, tourDone: false, tourSelection: null — User B is unaffected by User A's completion.
